Hi Ben — thanks for the quick follow-up and for the rate card. Good questions below and I tried to answer inline:

1) Our prefetch jobs do not return text to end-users. They advance the model state and persist KV snapshots into a short-term cache store so the first live request can be served from the cache.
2) We have ~8 stable prompt templates that are reused across sessions and an additional ~120 ad-hoc variants. The templates cover the primary user flows.
3) Prefetches are scheduled: we run a lightweight prewarm job every 30 minutes for high-traffic customer segments, and hourly for the rest.

What we'd like clarified from Redwood:
- Will those scheduled prefetch operations be billed the same as a normal generation (i.e., counted as generated tokens)?

Hi all — quick technical + billing summary based on Acme's usage sample and our hosted metering model. I'll keep this high-level but concrete so procurement can map to an invoice:

1) Two call types to consider:
   - Prefetch-only (no returned tokens): background job advances the KV cache and stores a snapshot.
   - Live-request (user-facing) that reuses cached KV state and returns tokens to the client.

2) How we charge today (hosted API):
   - Live-request tokens: billed per token at the published generation rate in the rate card (line: GENERATION-TOKENS).
   - Prefetch-only operations that do not emit tokens are metered as "cache precompute". Currently we do meter these because they consume GPU cycles; for hosted plans they appear as a separate SKU (CACHE-PRECOMPUTE) and are priced at a fractional rate relative to generation (example: 15% of the normal per-token compute cost, remapped to an estimated token-equivalent for invoicing). They do not generate normal token line items.
   - Cache hits on live-requests: we bill the actual tokens returned to the client. If the cached state reduces generation (fewer tokens produced), you'll see fewer GENERATION-TOKENS billed. We do not double-bill a "cache hit" and a generation charge for the same volume. The cache precompute SKU is only billed for the proactive precompute action.

3) Example invoice mapping (attached as ratecard_line_example.xlsx):
   - Line A: CACHE-PRECOMPUTE — 1,200 precompute units — $X (fractional compute rate)
   - Line B: GENERATION-TOKENS — 3,450,000 tokens returned to clients — $Y

4) Commercial proposal options for Acme's pilot:
   - Option 1: 90-day onboarding exemption on CACHE-PRECOMPUTE for up to 200k precompute units (we credit the SKU).
   - Option 2: 6-month discounted CACHE-PRECOMPUTE rate at 50% of published fractional rate for customers committing to a baseline monthly committed spend.
   - Option 3: No exemption, but offer a blended rate for total compute (combine CACHE-PRECOMPUTE + GENERATION-TOKENS into a single discounted per-token equivalent) for a committed monthly volume.

5) Remaining items we need from Acme to produce a firm proforma:
   - Typical precompute frequency per template and estimated average cost (your sample helps).
   - Targeted baseline commit (if you want Option 2 or 3).

I'll attach a simple spreadsheet that converts precompute minutes into the invoice SKU so procurement can see line-by-line math. Happy to hop on a short call with procurement to finalize the wording for the SOW/quote.
